# Tissametteyyamāṇavapucchā (Snp 5.3 (PTS Snp 199))

**ID:** Snp 5.3 (PTS Snp 199)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Tissametteyyamāṇavapucchā

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Tissametteyyamāṇavapucchā* ("The Questions of the Student Tissametteyya") is the third discourse of the *Pārāyanavagga* in the *Suttanipāta* (vv. 1040–1042, PTS Snp 199) [Anderson and Smith 1913; Norman 1997-2001; SuttaCentral]. Composed in Śloka metre, the sutta records an exchange between the Buddha and Tissa Metteyya, one of the disciples of the ascetic Bāvari [Goldstone 1978; Norman 1997-2001]. Tissa Metteyya inquires who in the world is free from tremors (*iñjitā*), who has known both ends and does not cling to the middle (*ubh' anta-m-abhiññāya majjhe mantā na lippati*), who is rightly called a "great person" (*mahāpurisa*), and who has overcome the seamstress of craving (*sibbanī*) [Anderson and Smith 1913; SuttaCentral]. While modern scholars frequently cite this text alongside other early suttas when investigating the early roots of the Maitreya narrative, the text itself focuses on attaining the desireless state and makes no reference to a future Buddha [Goldstone 1978].

Canonical commentary on the sutta is found in the *Cūḷaniddesa*, both in the general *Pucchā* (Cnd 2) and the dedicated *Tissametteyyamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 6) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus], while the traditional *aṭṭhakathā* exegesis is preserved in *Paramatthajotikā II* (Pj II 588–589) [Norman 1997-2001]. SuttaCentral identifies a thematic resembling parallel in the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (*Majjhesutta*, AN 6.61) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus indicates extensive internal reuse within the Pali canon, matching 35 passages with Cnd 6 (such as §1.1–2.5 with §8.3–10.5) and 5 passages with Cnd 2 [DharmaNexus]. Externally, Norman discusses a fragmentary Sanskrit text of the *Pārāyaṇa* traditions containing elements reminiscent of verse 1040, such as the term *mahāpuruṣa* [Norman 1997-2001]. DharmaNexus additionally computes low-similarity machine alignments with verses of the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (D0326) [DharmaNexus].
